subtitle: A book opens onto Ivalice

body: Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift is Square Enix's Nintendo DS tactical role-playing game about Luso Clemens, a boy drawn into Ivalice through a magical book. He joins a clan led by Cid and searches for a way home while becoming involved in its disputes and missions. Battles unfold on isometric grids, where the composition of the group matters before the first move. The book supplies the reason for entering another world; the clan provides a practical place within it, with work to accept and companions to develop.

The Job system gives clan members different combat roles and abilities. Equipment and development shape those choices, allowing the player to prepare a party for the demands of a mission. On the battlefield, position determines which targets and spaces can be reached during a turn. A well-built unit still needs a useful place to stand. The combination connects long-term character growth to short-term spatial decisions, so preparing a clan is not separate from its tactical life. It is the beginning of the next plan.

Battles can impose laws that restrict particular actions, requiring the player to adapt an otherwise comfortable approach. The rule gives a familiar group another problem to solve without replacing its abilities. Beyond the active party, clan members can be sent on training assignments or side missions, allowing the organisation to keep developing. Tactics A2 makes a substantial adventure from this routine of accepting work, preparing people and meeting conditions. Luso's search for home runs through a world in which a clan's everyday decisions create the substance of the journey.
